newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: U.S. holiday effectively closes Argentine bond mkt.
newsitem.headline: U.S. holiday effectively closes Argentine bond mkt.

text.p: Argentine bonds went untraded Friday because of the U.S. Independence Day holiday, dealers said.
Though the market was technically open, no new bid and offer ranges were being set, and the only business transacted were deals that need to be closed today.
"No prices are being set, so there won't be any business all day," one dealer said.
On Thursday, local bonds firmed but slipped off the day's highs in a lackluster session compared to the frenzy seen in the U.S. Treasuries market.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/8 to close at 94-1/2, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 added $0.10 to 121.50.

Traders said the favorable U.S. jobs report Thursday, which came on the heels of the Federal Reserve's decision not to touch interest rates, set the stage for fresh gains in fixed-income markets next week.
